User Story: As a user, I want to start an MRC update from an existing rate card so that I can preserve the current pricing structure while applying new changes.
UI Behavior: The user can select an existing MRC and choose Clone or Create New Version.
Backend/System Behavior: The system creates a working copy of the selected rate card and preserves the original version.
Acceptance Criteria: The original MRC remains unchanged and the new version has its own identifier or version number.

User Story: As a user, I want to review MRC pricing by product, weight, zone, tier, and geography so that I can understand the recommended changes.
UI Behavior: The UI provides table and pivot-style views, with navigation for applicable tiers and geographies.
Backend/System Behavior: The application retrieves the appropriate rate-card rows and supporting pricing information from the prepared data store.
Acceptance Criteria: The user can view the affected pricing rows and identify the applicable product, weight, zone, tier, and geography.

User Story: As a user, I want to use plain language to request targeted MRC changes so that I can update groups of cells without editing them individually.
UI Behavior: The user can enter an instruction to change rates for selected zones, products, weights, or geographies. The user can request either a flat amount change or a percentage change.
Backend/System Behavior: The AI agent interprets the request and creates a proposed set of changes for the selected MRC.
Acceptance Criteria: The proposed changes are limited to the requested scope and are shown before they are applied. For example, the user can request, 'Increase Zones 5 through 8 by $0.25 for packages between 1 and 3 pounds,' or 'Increase all Zone 6 rates by 5 percent.'

User Story: As a user, I want the system to ask clarifying questions when my MRC request is unclear so that the wrong rates are not changed.
UI Behavior: The UI displays questions when the request does not identify a complete scope, such as the product, zone, weight range, or geography.
Backend/System Behavior: The system does not apply changes until the request has enough information to identify the affected rows.
Acceptance Criteria: The user can provide clarification and receive an updated change preview.

User Story: As a user, I want MRC changes to respect pricing limits so that a recommended or manually requested price does not violate established rules.
UI Behavior: The UI explains when a requested change exceeds an applicable limit and prevents or requires clarification before continuing.
Backend/System Behavior: The system checks the proposed price against applicable published-rate and price-floor rules. For MRC pricing, the published rate is the ceiling for the applicable product, weight, zone, or other rate-card cell. MRC prices should not exceed the applicable published rate and should not fall below an applicable price floor.
Acceptance Criteria: The system does not apply an MRC change that violates an applicable price floor or ceiling. If a requested change would exceed the published rate or fall below the price floor, the user receives an explanation and must revise or clarify the request.

User Story: As a user, I want to review and approve only the impacted MRC rows as a group so that I can confirm the changes without reviewing every unchanged cell.
UI Behavior: The UI displays only the impacted rows. The UI provides clear actions to Approve, Reject, or Revise the proposed changes.
Backend/System Behavior: The system stores the impacted rows as a reviewable change set and does not require unchanged rows to be reviewed individually.
Acceptance Criteria: The user can review only the impacted rows. The UI provides Approve, Reject, and Revise actions. Approve requires the user to enter a valid future effective date and confirm that the approved rates will be sent to Panorama. Reject discards the proposed changes. Revise returns the user to the editing process. No changes are sent to Panorama until approval is completed.

User Story: As a user, I want approved MRC changes to be sent to Panorama so that the new merchant prices can be used by the appropriate pricing systems.
UI Behavior: The UI changes the MRC status to Approved or Ready to Send after approval and indicates that the rates are being sent to Panorama.
Backend/System Behavior: The system creates an approved MRC output and places it in the outbound processing area for transmission to Panorama.
Acceptance Criteria: Only approved MRC versions are sent to Panorama. The transmission includes the approved rate-card version, effective date, customer, contract, and impacted pricing rows. The system records whether Panorama accepted or rejected the update.

User Story: As a user, I want the system to create the applicable platform rate cards from an approved MRC so that I do not have to manually create separate rate cards for every platform.
UI Behavior: The UI indicates that approval of the MRC completes the user-facing portion of the process. The UI does not display PRC creation or commission recalculation status after approval.
Backend/System Behavior: The system uses the approved MRC and the applicable commission information from Panorama to create or update PRCs. PRCs that are exempt, excluded, or otherwise designated as disregarded are not created or updated.
Acceptance Criteria: The resulting PRCs are linked to the source MRC. Applicable PRCs are created for the appropriate platforms and products. PRCs designated as disregarded are excluded from processing and identified in the backend record.

User Story: As a user, I want the system to use commission information stored in Panorama so that each platform rate card reflects the correct platform agreement.
UI Behavior: The UI does not display the commission information retrieval or recalculation activity after the MRC is approved.
Backend/System Behavior: The system retrieves the applicable commission information from Panorama and uses it to recalculate the platform pricing.
Acceptance Criteria: The calculation uses the correct customer, platform, contract, commission information, and MRC version. The calculation is performed entirely in the backend.
Notes: New PRC Rate Cell Price = New MRC Rate Cell Price ? (New MRC Rate Cell Price × Commission Percentage)

User Story: As a user, I want platform commissions to be recalculated automatically after an approved MRC update so that platform pricing stays aligned with the updated merchant prices.
UI Behavior: The UI does not display the commission recalculation status or require the user to review the generated PRCs after the MRC is approved.
Backend/System Behavior: The system identifies affected platforms, retrieves commission information from Panorama, recalculates applicable PRC values, and identifies PRCs that must be disregarded based on configured rules.
Acceptance Criteria: Every applicable PRC receives a recalculated result or a clearly identified backend exception. PRCs that are designated to be disregarded are recorded and excluded from the recalculation or publication process. The calculation uses the correct customer, platform, contract, commission information, and MRC version.

User Story: As a user, I want the system to create the required platform rate-card versions after recalculating commissions so that Panorama receives complete and accurate platform pricing data.
UI Behavior: The UI does not display the generated PRC versions or their processing status after the MRC is approved.
Backend/System Behavior: The system creates the applicable platform rate-card outputs using the recalculated platform values and prepares them for transmission to Panorama.
Acceptance Criteria: Each applicable PRC identifies the source MRC, platform, customer or contract, effective date, and calculation version. Disregarded PRCs are excluded. The approved PRC outputs are sent to Panorama.

User Story: As a user, I want platform-rate exceptions and disregarded PRCs to be handled automatically so that unusual customer or commission arrangements do not produce incorrect platform pricing.
UI Behavior: The UI does not display discarded or disregarded PRC versions, commission exceptions, or backend PRC processing results after the MRC is approved.
Backend/System Behavior: The system identifies missing commission information, unsupported customer arrangements, calculation differences, and other special cases. It stops or excludes affected PRCs from processing and records the reason in the backend.
Acceptance Criteria: Disregarded PRCs are not created, sent to Panorama, or presented as available rate-card versions. The backend records the affected customer or platform, source MRC, reason for being disregarded, and processing status.

User Story: As a user, I want to start a TLPC update from the applicable customer contract rate card so that the temporary change is based on the correct contract pricing.
UI Behavior: The UI allows the user to select the applicable customer, contract, product, and base rate template.
Backend/System Behavior: The system retrieves the customer's official pre-TLPC contract pricing from the applicable template or Panorama data.
Acceptance Criteria: The TLPC update is linked to the correct customer, contract, base pricing template, and effective period.

User Story: As a user, I want to apply a TLPC increase to a selected group of products, weights, zones, tiers, or geographies so that I can make targeted changes without editing every cell.
UI Behavior: The UI supports selecting or describing a specific range, such as selected products, weights, zones, or tiers.
Backend/System Behavior: The system applies the requested adjustment only to the selected rate-card rows.
Acceptance Criteria: Rows outside the requested scope remain unchanged.

User Story: As a user, I want to apply a percentage or fixed adjustment to a group of TLPC rates so that I can process negotiated changes efficiently.
UI Behavior: The UI allows the user to specify an adjustment type, such as a percentage or fixed amount, and the affected range.
Backend/System Behavior: The system calculates the adjusted values for the selected rows and creates a preview.
Acceptance Criteria: The preview clearly shows the original value, adjustment, and resulting value for each affected group.

User Story: As a user, I want a TLPC to have a defined start and end date so that the temporary pricing automatically applies only during the approved period.
UI Behavior: The UI requires an effective start date and may require an end date for the TLPC.
Backend/System Behavior: The system stores the TLPC period and associates it with the applicable contract and rate-card version.
Acceptance Criteria: The TLPC is active only during the approved period. The system applies the appropriate contract pricing after the TLPC period ends, according to the applicable contract rules.

User Story: As a user, I want to review a complete TLPC change preview before approval so that I can confirm that the negotiated adjustment was applied correctly.
UI Behavior: The UI displays affected rows and final TLPC value.
Backend/System Behavior: The system creates a reviewable calculation result before updating the rate card.
Acceptance Criteria: The user can approve, reject, or revise the TLPC change before it is published.

User Story: As a user, I want approved TLPC rates to be sent to Panorama so that Panorama and related pricing systems use the approved temporary rates.
UI Behavior: The UI allows the user to approve the TLPC update but does not display post-approval publication status or transmission results.
Backend/System Behavior: The system creates an approved TLPC output and makes it available for transmission to Panorama.
Acceptance Criteria: The approved TLPC rate card is sent to Panorama with the customer, contract, effective period, and version information. The system records whether Panorama accepted or rejected the update in the backend.

User Story: As a user, I want the system to clearly identify whether I am working with an MRC or TLPC so that I understand the rules and workflow that apply.
UI Behavior: The UI displays the rate-card type, workflow status, effective dates, and available actions.
Backend/System Behavior: The system applies the correct processing rules based on the rate-card type.
Acceptance Criteria: The user cannot accidentally process an MRC or TLPC using the wrong workflow.

User Story: As a user, I want rate-card updates to be protected from conflicting edits so that another user does not overwrite my work.
UI Behavior: The UI shows when a rate card is being reviewed or locked and informs the user when another person has an active edit session.
Backend/System Behavior: The system temporarily locks the working rate card or detects conflicting versions before saving changes.
Acceptance Criteria: Conflicting changes are prevented or presented to the user for resolution.

User Story: As a user, I want to approve a rate-card update and understand that it will be processed by Panorama so that I know when my user-facing work is complete.
UI Behavior: The UI displays the rate-card type, effective date, and approval confirmation before the user submits the update. After approval, the UI does not display downstream processing statuses, commission recalculation results, or Panorama transmission results.
Backend/System Behavior: The backend updates the rate-card status and continues the integration process through outbound processing and Panorama. Any downstream status, commission recalculation, exception, or transmission result is maintained in the backend.
Acceptance Criteria: The user must provide the required effective date and confirm approval. After approval, the backend continues processing without requiring additional UI action. Downstream processing results are recorded in the backend.
